messages:
oliver: Heads-up — noticed the console is showing both v1 and v2 badges for the same route in a few tenants. UX looks confusing to customers.

sujata: can you paste a screenshot or tenant id? curious if this is a display bug or real dual routing.

oliver: tenant: acme-payments, screenshot attached (uploaded). Appears under Routes -> /generate: shows v2 'recommended' badge but traffic graph still 100% v1.

aj: that sounds like a telemetry join issue — console is querying config store for pinned variant and router metrics separately. if timing mismatch, badges could be stale.

maria: agree. current badge logic is: show preferredVariant from console cache OR highlight if route recentRollout > 0. If metrics say otherwise we add a small note. This thread makes me think we need a stronger precedence rule.

kevin: @aj any chance the router emits a different variant tag than the metrics pipeline expects? we had a tag rename last quarter.

aj: good point. router emits header: X-Variant=v2-beta for canary. metrics pipeline normalizes to 'v2'. normalization table updated but I don't think it covers the 'v2-beta' suffix.

linda: analytics side: metrics come with variant_label field. we run a map step that reduces known variants, unknowns go to 'other'. If router sends unexpected suffix we map to 'other' which then doesn't match console config.

oliver: Customers interpret this as 'console lied' which is bad. Proposal: console should compute badge from merged view: if recent traffic (>1% in last 5m) is on v1, show v1 as active even if config says preferred v2. Or add a small tooltip explaining discrepancy.

sujata: UX + product: tooltip is low friction. But long-term we prefer deterministic precedence. I'd vote: metrics > config for the active badge (so what is actually serving wins), config shown as "preferred" label.

maria: implementation detail: we already fetch metrics async — switching precedence means we must wait for metrics read to render initial state or render a loading stub. that changes performance characteristics.

aj: alternative: show both but add an inline confidence meter: green if metrics+config agree, amber if mismatch and metrics show <5% skew, red if >20% skew. that avoids blocking render.

kevin: from infra side, adding more real-time reads will increase read QPS on metrics store. Need a cost estimate.

linda: metrics query per-route per-tenant is expensive at scale. We can approximate with sampled counters that are already emitted by router (per-tenant per-variant counters). cheap option: query the router counter shard instead of full-timeseries.

maria: ok plan sketch: 1) add confidence meter UI 2) read fast counters (router shard) for initial badge state 3) enrich tooltip with last-5m percent per-variant 4) background reconcile with TSDB for historical context

sujata: product thumbs-up on that flow. timeline?

aj: engineer estimate: prototyping UI + router-counter read 2w, backend QA + rollout 1w, console flag + gradual rollout 1w. total ~4w.

oliver: edge case: tenants with pinned model versions (tenant pin overrides routing). Badges must reflect pin policy. If tenant pins v1 but global preferred is v2, UI should clearly show "pinned" label.

maria: noted — we already show a lock icon for pins but it's not prominent. We'll change copy to "Pinned to v1 by tenant" and color it distinct from 'preferred'.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: console/ui-service v2.14.7 -> canary (hosts: console-canary-3). sha: ab12cde.

aj: thanks deploy-bot — reminder to add a small feature flag behind `console.variant_confidence_ui`. We'll enable for internal-orgs first.

linda: telemetry follow-up: I'll add mapping rule for variant suffixes (v2-*, v2beta -> v2) on ingestion path to avoid 'other' buckets. That will reduce false mismatches.

kevin: also recommend adding an opt-in debug banner (for internal) that shows raw variant_label from router + normalized label so we can audit mismatches quickly.

oliver: this feels good. Last ask: can we add a dashboard tile for "variant mismatches" (count of routes where config != serving) so PMs can track migration health?

sujata: yes please. PMs will use that metric to decide when to pause rollouts.

maria: I'll add a small card in the Route Health dashboard: mismatches (5m), top tenants, and recent examples.

aj: action items recap: @maria implement confidence UI + pin copy change (2w), @linda ingest mapping for suffixes (1w), @aj add router-counter read endpoint + opt-in debug banner (2w), @kevin capacity check on router counter QPS (ASAP), @sujata create PM ticket for dashboard tile.

oliver: thanks all. if anyone hits a snag ping me. :thumbsup:

maria: will post a short PR when UI prototype ready.

deploy-bot: canary deployment completed: console/ui-service v2.14.7 on console-canary-3 succeeded.

linda: I'll monitor mismatch metric and post a baseline report tomorrow morning.
